title: Day 72: Trump Rejects Iran Counter-Proposal as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' — Ceasefire Increasingly Shaky; Iran Calls Its Terms 'Reasonable'
detail: On May 11, 2026 (Day 72 of the US-Iran war), President Trump publicly rejected Iran's counter-proposal — submitted via Pakistani intermediaries on May 10 — posting on Truth Social that it was 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' and accusing Tehran of 'playing games.' Iran's counter-proposal included: recognition of Iranian sovereignty and management over the Strait of Hormuz as a precondition; refusal to dismantle nuclear facilities (insisting nuclear talks be handled on a separate track); an offer to halt uranium enrichment for a shorter period than the US demanded and to send some highly enriched uranium to a third country while diluting the rest; lifting of OFAC sanctions on Iranian oil sales within 30 days; release of frozen Iranian assets; compensation for war damages; and an end to fighting on all fronts including Lebanon. The US 14-point proposal had demanded a 12–15 year moratorium on uranium enrichment, Iran handing over ~440 kg of 60%-enriched uranium, gradual sanctions lifting, and gradual Hormuz reopening during a 30-day negotiation window. Iran's Foreign Ministry said its counter-proposal was 'reasonable' and called Trump's rejection a sign of bad faith. Iran warned it would 'confront its enemies' if negotiations collapsed. CNN's live blog and Washington Post described the US-Iran ceasefire — which had nominally been in place since April 7 — as 'increasingly shaky' following Trump's rejection. Pakistan's FM Ishaq Dar said intermediary contacts were continuing despite the setback. Qatar's parallel mediation channel also remained active. Brent crude spiked back toward $108–112/bbl on the news, reversing the modest peace-optimism easing from May 10. The US naval blockade of Iranian ports remained in place with roughly 31 tankers (~53 million barrels) still blocked; approximately 22,500 mariners remained trapped on 1,550+ vessels.

media.caption: Trump rejects Iran's counter-proposal as 'TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE!' — US-Iran ceasefire grows increasingly shaky on Day 72 of the war, May 11, 2026

title: Russia-Ukraine 72-Hour Ceasefire Expires Day 3 With No Extension — Russia Claims 16,071 Violations; Kharkiv Struck; Geneva Talks Status Unclear
detail: The US-brokered 72-hour Russia-Ukraine ceasefire (May 9–11, 2026) expired on May 11 with no announced extension, as both sides traded blame for violations throughout the pause. Russia claimed Ukraine violated the ceasefire 16,071 times during the three-day window and that it 'strictly observed' the agreement — a claim Ukraine flatly rejected. Ukraine documented continued Russian frontline ground combat throughout the ceasefire, and on the final day Russia carried out a drone strike on a high-rise building in Kharkiv, injuring at least 5 people including two 8-year-old children. Separate Russian strikes on the Kherson and Dnipropetrovsk regions killed at least 2 civilians — including a 46-year-old woman — and wounded 7 others. Russia had also fired 43 drones and an Iskander-M ballistic missile in the opening hours of the ceasefire (May 9 overnight), and later launched 27 long-range drones. The 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange that was part of the ceasefire deal was reported as proceeding despite the fighting. With the ceasefire expired, US and European officials were described by the Washington Post as 'considering how they might steer the warring countries into further talks.' The Geneva peace talks — where European leaders, Canada, and Australia had been invited to join broader negotiations scheduled for the week of May 12 — remained in an uncertain status. Putin had publicly expressed willingness to meet Zelensky 'after a full peace treaty,' but Russia's conditions — including that Ukraine withdraw from Donetsk areas Russia failed to capture militarily — remained unacceptable to Kyiv. NATO allies warned that any settlement at current frontlines without adequate security guarantees would reward Russian aggression.

media.caption: Russia-Ukraine 72-hour ceasefire expires with no extension — both sides trade blame; Russia claims 16,071 violations; Kharkiv struck on final day, May 11, 2026

title: Senate Clears Cloture on Kevin Warsh Fed Chair Nomination (5:30 PM ET) — Final Confirmation Vote Imminent; Powell Exits May 15
detail: The United States Senate held a cloture vote at 5:30 p.m. ET on May 11, 2026 on Kevin Warsh's nomination as Federal Reserve Chair, clearing the procedural hurdle that paved the way for a final confirmation floor vote later in the week. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) had filed cloture on April 30, with the Senate Daily Press schedule confirming two roll call votes for May 11: the cloture motion on Warsh as Member of the Board of Governors (Executive Calendar #728) and a separate cloture filing on #727 (Chairman of the Board). With Republicans holding a 53-seat Senate majority and Sen. John Fetterman (D-PA) expected to support Warsh alongside the Republican caucus, confirmation was widely viewed as near-certain. Warsh had cleared the Senate Banking Committee on April 29 in a 13–11 party-line vote — the first fully partisan Fed Chair committee vote in modern history, according to former Fed economist Claudia Sahm. The cloture vote advancement set up Warsh's final floor confirmation before the expiration of Jerome Powell's term as Fed Chair on May 15, 2026. Powell confirmed he would remain on the Fed's Board of Governors as a governor after stepping down as Chair. Warsh, a former Fed governor (2006–2011) and Morgan Stanley investment banker, has signaled openness to interest rate cuts and closer coordination with the White House — positions that have drawn criticism from Democratic senators and some mainstream economists who warn of threats to Fed independence. His first FOMC meeting as Chair was expected at the June 16–17 meeting, where markets anticipated the Fed could signal its first rate cut since the Iran war began.

media.caption: Senate clears cloture on Kevin Warsh Fed Chair nomination at 5:30 PM ET — final confirmation vote imminent before Powell's May 15 exit, May 11, 2026

title: China Officially Confirms Trump State Visit to Beijing May 13–15 — Xi-Trump Summit to Cover Iran War, Trade Truce, Taiwan, Rare Earths
detail: China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs officially announced on May 11, 2026 that 'At the invitation of President Xi Jinping, President Donald Trump of the United States of America will pay a state visit to China from May 13 to 15' — confirming Trump's first visit to China and the first US presidential visit in nearly nine years. The trip had been delayed from an originally planned early April date due to the active US-Iran war. The confirmed itinerary included a welcome ceremony, bilateral meetings with President Xi Jinping on May 14, a visit to the Temple of Heaven, a state banquet, and bilateral tea and a working lunch before Trump's departure on May 15. Key agenda items confirmed by multiple sources: (1) Iran war and Strait of Hormuz reopening — both the US and China want the strait reopened, as a fifth of global oil and gas previously transited it and the blockade has severely disrupted Chinese energy imports; (2) extension of the US-China trade truce reached in South Korea in late 2025, which had rolled back export controls including on rare earth shipments vital for US defense manufacturing, semiconductors, and consumer electronics; (3) Taiwan; and (4) the case of Hong Kong pro-democracy activist Jimmy Lai, which was reportedly on the US side's agenda. The Bloomberg headline on May 11 was 'China Confirms Xi-Trump Summit After Delay Linked to Iran War.' The Washington Post noted that Xi was 'confident in China's power' and described both leaders approaching the summit from positions of strength. The timing was geopolitically significant: Trump was simultaneously rejecting Iran's counter-proposal and dealing with the expiration of the Russia-Ukraine ceasefire — making the Beijing summit a pivotal moment in global diplomacy.

media.caption: China confirms Trump state visit May 13-15; Xi-Trump summit agenda covers Iran war, trade truce extension, rare earths, Taiwan, and Jimmy Lai, May 11, 2026
